build(cpp): requalify the integrated native gateway on Apple Silicon

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-f1-20261118-44343309770-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), ICU for Unicode, and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). Your branch will be merged with theirs: stay strictly inside your OWNED PATHS and keep everything else byte-identical.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted macOS runner on Apple Silicon (Homebrew available, no apt). `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md` and `cpp/gateway/tools/macos-build.sh` are a verified recipe from an earlier state of the tree (441 of 441 binaries, 5,029 cases): follow them, they list the Homebrew packages and the SQLite 3.54.0 preparation.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these, plus your report)
- `cpp/gateway/tools/macos-build.sh`, `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md`, Darwin-guarded (`#if defined(__APPLE__)`) branches anywhere under `cpp/gateway/include`, `cpp/gateway/src`, `cpp/gateway/tests`, and non-guarded changes only when they are standard-library portability fixes that cannot change Linux behaviour (a missing include, an implicit conversion Apple Clang rejects)

TASK
Since the macOS recipe last passed (442 binaries, 5,034 cases on Apple Silicon, report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-macos-requal-20261118.md`), this branch integrated many library replacements: llhttp (HTTP request and response parsing), Ada (URL), QCBOR (passkey CBOR), OpenSSL ASN.1/X.509 decoding, Boost.Multiprecision BigInt, Boost.Beast outbound WebSocket, standard-library helpers for console/headers/multipart/environment/filesystem/containers/gzip, stored-value reader fixes, a JSON depth cap, and a release packaging pipeline (`cpp/gateway/packaging/macos/build.py`, `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-release.yml`). The integration was verified on Linux ARM64 only (450 binaries, 5,104 cases; report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-f1-20261118.md`). Bring the macOS build back to green on this branch: update `tools/macos-build.sh` so it builds and links every vendored library now registered (`tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`), build every production source with Apple Clang and libc++, run the runtime tests first and then the whole suite, and fix what fails within your owned paths. Under the owner policy, a test that fails only because a recorded quirk differs on Darwin gets a Darwin-conditional expectation; a functional failure gets a fix or, if it is outside your paths, a precise report. Then run `python3 -B cpp/gateway/packaging/macos/build.py` as the release workflow's macOS job does and confirm the package still builds and answers `--version`. Record binaries and cases passed. Commit after every fix: your process can be restarted without warning, and after a restart you must read your report and `git log` first.

DONE WHEN
`tools/macos-build.sh` builds everything from a clean checkout on your runner and the full suite passes, or every remaining failure is listed with its first error lines and a diagnosis; the macOS package builds.
